Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates an LLM’s ability to solve real GitHub issues by producing a code patch that passes repository tests, with problems curated to be solvable and verified by human review. It measures end-to-end software engineering skill including understanding the bug report, navigating a codebase, and implementing a correct fix under single-attempt settings when used as pass@1.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor), Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style issue-resolution to multiple programming languages, testing whether models can generalize software engineering competence beyond Python. Tasks require reading repository context, writing patches, and satisfying language-specific tooling and test suites across diverse ecosystems.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a harder, more contamination-resistant software engineering benchmark designed to reflect realistic industrial tasks across multiple languages and larger, more complex repos. It emphasizes robust patch generation, deeper codebase understanding, and higher difficulty issue types than SWE-bench Verified.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic performance on real command-line tasks inside sandboxed environments, where models must use shell commands and tools to complete objectives. It stresses iterative debugging, environment state tracking, and correct sequencing of actions under resource and time constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: BrowseComp evaluates “deep research” agents that must answer questions by searching and synthesizing information from the web (or a controlled corpus, depending on the setup). It tests tool use for retrieval, evidence integration, and maintaining task focus across multi-step browsing workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: τ2-bench measures an agent’s ability to complete multi-turn customer-support style tasks by interacting with simulated users and programmatic APIs while following domain policies. It probes robustness in dialogue, tool calling, and policy adherence across environments such as retail, airline, and telecom.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension, Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: OSWorld evaluates multimodal computer-use agents operating in desktop-like environments, requiring screenshot understanding and actions such as clicking, typing, and navigation to accomplish tasks. It stresses long-horizon planning, interface grounding, and error recovery in interactive GUI settings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Working Memory, Sensorimotor Coordination (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid-intelligence benchmark where models infer latent rules from a small set of input–output grid examples and must generate the correct output for new inputs. It aims to minimize reliance on memorized domain knowledge and instead emphasize novel pattern induction and abstraction.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence and strategy in a simulated vending-machine business over extended time (e.g., a year), scoring models by business outcomes such as final balance. It requires sustained goal pursuit, inventory and pricing decisions, and adaptation to changing simulated conditions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas assesses real-world tool use via the Model Context Protocol by requiring models to discover tools, call them with correct schemas, handle errors, and compose multi-step workflows across servers. It targets practical agent reliability in production-like API environments rather than purely textual QA.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates performance on tasks typical of an entry-level financial analyst, often requiring tool use (e.g., spreadsheets, calculations, retrieval) and structured deliverables. It emphasizes quantitative reasoning, following finance-domain conventions, and producing coherent analyses under constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity capability at scale on tasks such as finding known vulnerabilities in real open-source projects and, in some settings, discovering new issues. It stresses reading and reasoning over code, identifying exploit-relevant patterns, and producing actionable technical outputs under pass@1 evaluation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench measures an agent’s ability to understand, edit, and compute over complex spreadsheets drawn from realistic scenarios. Tasks probe formula reasoning, data manipulation, formatting, and multi-step transformations using spreadsheet tooling or programmatic libraries.
Cognitive Functions:

Cognitive Functions:

L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning (minor)

L1:

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU-style subject exams to multiple languages, testing whether models maintain broad academic knowledge and reasoning performance beyond English. It typically uses multiple-choice questions across many disciplines and evaluates cross-lingual generalization.
Cognitive Functions:

L3:

It evaluates visual grounding, cross-modal reasoning, and the ability to extract structured information from visuals.

It emphasizes robust visual reasoning and higher-level cross-modal understanding rather than surface recognition.
Cognitive Functions:

L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Working Memory (minor), Logical Reasoning (minor)

Cognitive Functions:

L1:

L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Global PIQA evaluates pragmatic physical commonsense and everyday reasoning across many languages and cultural contexts, often by choosing the most plausible solution or explanation. Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) evaluates long-context multi-round coreference resolution by embedding repeated, similar “needle” requests in a long “haystack” dialogue and asking the model to reproduce the correct response associated with a specified needle. Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Working Memory, Attention
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates well-specified professional knowledge-work tasks across many occupations (e.g., creating spreadsheets, presentations, schedules, diagrams), graded by expert human judges via pairwise comparisons. Cognitive Functions:
L1:

L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: Graphwalks tests whether models can perform structured traversal and query tasks over graphs described in text, such as following edges, finding parents, or executing BFS-like reasoning.
